EO 13286 section 49 replaced the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security, effective 2003-03-01; the delegation continues in the current U.S. Code note. No held source ends it.

Section 1-101(b) delegated to the U.S. Coordinator for Refugee Affairs the functions of reporting and periodic discussions under section 207(d)(1). EO 13286 section 49 (68 FR 10619, signed 2003-02-28) amends EO 12208 by 'striking sections 1–101(b) and 1–102', and section 92 provides 'This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003.' The end is therefore dated 2003-03-01 (the effective date; the signing date 2003-02-28 is the exclusive alternative reading). The current U.S. Code note for 8 U.S.C. 1157 no longer prints this provision, which confirms the strike took effect.

The end is therefore dated 2003-03-01 (the effective date; the signing date 2003-02-28 is the exclusive alternative reading). The current U.S. Code note for 8 U.S.C. 1157 no longer prints this provision, which confirms the strike took effect.

The end is therefore dated 2003-03-01 (the effective date; the signing date 2003-02-28 is the exclusive alternative reading). research_rationale:
EO 12208 (45 FR 25789, signed 1980-04-15; FR Doc. 80-11908) delegates to the Secretary of State and the Attorney General the functions of consulting with the Judiciary Committees under sections 101(a)(42)(B) and 207(a), (b), (d) and (e) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, delegates to the U.S. Coordinator for Refugee Affairs the reporting and discussion functions of section 207(d)(1) and directs how the Coordinator acts and notifies the Committees, reserves to the President the determinations and refugee-number decisions under sections 101(a)(42)(B) and 207, and deems earlier actions taken under delegated functions to have been taken under the order. Identity: the held Federal Register text of 45 FR 25789-25790 (PDF pages 11-12) prints 'Consultations on the Admission of Refugees' and 'April 15, 1980'. The inventory is corrected to ten clauses (see the inventory reason). Later events: EO 12608 (52 FR 34617, signed 1987-09-09), section 15, lists EO 12208 among the orders in which the words Department of Health, Education, and Welfare and Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare are replaced by the Department and Secretary of Health and Human Services; the only such reference in EO 12208 is in section 1-102(a). EO 13286 (68 FR 10619, effective 2003-03-01 by its section 92), section 49, strikes the words that introduce 1-101(a) and replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security in 1-101(a); strikes sections 1-101(b) and 1-102; and redesignates sections 1-103 and 1-104 as 1-102 and 1-103. Result at 2026-10-14: sections 1-101(b), 1-102(a) and 1-102(b) (the Coordinator's functions) ended on 2003-03-01 by EO 13286; the delegation in 1-101 and (a), the reserved functions in 1-103 and the deemed-actions sentence in 1-104 continue, amended and renumbered, as the current U.S. Code note shows. No held source revokes the order.

No earlier revocation, supersession or own-terms end exists; the order has no sunset. It continues as section 1-103 and has no ending event in any held source.","scope_check":"EO 13286 section 49 acts on named sections only: it ends 1-101(b) and 1-102, amends 1-101 and 1-101(a), and renumbers 1-103 and 1-104. savings.reason: Section 1-104 (redesignated 1-103 by EO 13286) deems all prior actions under any delegated or assigned function to have been taken under the order, except to the extent inconsistent with it. It is a validation sentence that continues in the current text as printed in the U.S. Code note, so actions taken before the 2003 strike remain validated. The functions struck on 2003-03-01 (the Coordinator's) leave no held residual command.
